patch.description:
Update the content of a dataset.

The `index` and `column_name` fields are treated as keys tied to a specific version of the dataset.
As such, these values are considered immutable identifiers for the dataset's structure.

Edits are applied sequentially in list order, and each edit sees the table state left by the
previous one. For example, after a `rename_column` edit renames `col_a` to `col_b`, any
subsequent `update_row` in the same request must reference the column as `col_b`, not `col_a`.

The `If-Match` header is used to ensure that updates are only applied if the client's version of the dataset
matches the server's version. This prevents conflicts from simultaneous updates. The `ETag` header in the response
provides the new version identifier after a successful update.

Generate improved scorer prompt using Autotune (CLHF).

This endpoint:
1. Fetches all feedback items from the active queue with ClickHouse context
2. Assembles the current metric system prompt
3. Constructs AutotuneInput with annotated examples
4. Queues a background job to the runners service
5. Returns task_id for polling

The API prepares all data internally - no request body needed.

**Validation:**
- Scorer exists and user has access
- Active queue exists in 'pending' state
- Queue has at least one feedback item

**Response:**
- 202 Accepted with task_id for polling

**Errors:**
- 404 - Scorer not found or no active pending queue exists
- 409 - Queue is already locked (generating or reviewing)
- 422 - Scorer missing required configuration or queue has no feedback items

Returns only queue metadata (status, error message, draft prompt) without

**Errors:**

patch.description:
Update a feedback queue by performing an action.

**Supported actions:**
- "abort": Abort the feedback application process and return the queue to pending state.
  Used when user clicks "Back" or "Cancel" during generation or review.
  Clears draft_prompt and generation_task_id. Same queue is reused.
  Can be called during 'generating' or 'reviewing' state.

- "complete": Complete the queue after saving a new scorer version.
  Used when user saves a new version from the review flow.
  Sets status to completed (immutable) and links queue to the resulting version.
  Requires target_scorer_version_id, result_scorer_id, and result_scorer_version_id.
  Can only be called during 'reviewing' state.

**Request body:**
- action: The action to perform ("abort" or "complete")
- target_scorer_version_id: Required for "complete" action - ID of the version feedback was applied to
- result_scorer_id: Required for "complete" action - ID of the scorer that owns the result version.
  For custom LLM scorers this is the same as the queue's scorer. For preset scorers this is the
  new custom scorer duplicated from the preset.
- result_scorer_version_id: Required for "complete" action - ID of the scorer version created

**Response:**
- 200 OK with queue details showing updated status

**Errors:**
- 404 - Queue not found or user doesn't have access
- 409 - Queue is not in a valid state for the requested action
- 422 - Invalid action or missing required parameters

post.description:
Test a draft prompt against feedback records in the active queue.

Creates a metrics testing run by copying the feedback records and running
generated scorer validation with the provided prompt. Used in the AutoTune
Data tab for 3-column comparison: Original | Expected (Annotated) | New Result.

Works in any active queue state (pending, generating, or reviewing).

**Response:**
- 202 Accepted with metrics_testing_run_id for viewing results

**Errors:**
- 404 - Scorer not found or no active queue exists
- 422 - Queue has no feedback items or scorer has no version
- 500 - Record processing failure

get.description:
Poll autotune validation results for a feedback queue.

Returns one row per feedback item with the new scorer output joined in from
the metrics testing run. Used by the UI for the 3-column comparison table:
Original Value | Expected (Annotated) | New Result.

**Pollable:** Returns status=pending with null scores while validation is running.
Transitions through pending → in_progress → completed as scores arrive.

**Args:**
- metrics_testing_run_id: Optional metrics testing run ID (from validate response).
  When provided, fetches scored records and joins with feedback items.

**Errors:**
- 404 - Queue not found or user doesn't have access

If no admin exists (first user), the user will be created as an admin.

Otherwise:
- User record was already created when the admin invited the user
- We should verify the user's email

Create a user using a social login provider.

All social users are created with `email_is_verified=True`, don't need to be invited and are by default read-only
(unless they are the first user, in which case they are set to admin).

Exchange a refresh token cookie for a fresh access token, rotating the refresh token.

Verification reads through the writer session: every exchange stamps a new jti on the system user,
and the next exchange has to observe that write to accept the token it just handed out.

patch.description:
Update the content of a dataset.

The `index` and `column_name` fields are treated as keys tied to a specific version of the dataset.
As such, these values are considered immutable identifiers for the dataset's structure.

Edits are applied sequentially in list order, and each edit sees the table state left by the
previous one. For example, after a `rename_column` edit renames `col_a` to `col_b`, any
subsequent `update_row` in the same request must reference the column as `col_b`, not `col_a`.

The `If-Match` header is used to ensure that updates are only applied if the client's version of the dataset
matches the server's version. This prevents conflicts from simultaneous updates. The `ETag` header in the response
provides the new version identifier after a successful update.

patch.description:
Update the content of a dataset.

The `index` and `column_name` fields are treated as keys tied to a specific version of the dataset.
As such, these values are considered immutable identifiers for the dataset's structure.

Edits are applied sequentially in list order, and each edit sees the table state left by the
previous one. For example, after a `rename_column` edit renames `col_a` to `col_b`, any
subsequent `update_row` in the same request must reference the column as `col_b`, not `col_a`.

The `If-Match` header is used to ensure that updates are only applied if the client's version of the dataset
matches the server's version. This prevents conflicts from simultaneous updates. The `ETag` header in the response
provides the new version identifier after a successful update.

schema.description: ETag of the dataset as a version identifier.

parameters.description: ETag of the dataset as a version identifier.

412.description: ETag mismatch; client's If-Match does not match current resource version

423.description: Resource lock could not be acquired; another update may be in progress

CategoricalColorConstraint-Output.title: CategoricalColorConstraint
CategoricalColorConstraint-Output.description:
A color constraint for categorical or multi-label metric values.

Assigns a color when a categorical score matches the given operator and value.

Operators and expected value shapes:
  - eq: value must be a single string.
  - one_of: value must be a list of strings.

Example:

    {"color": "red", "operator": "one_of", "value": ["fail", "error"]}

DashboardConfigResponse.title: DashboardConfigResponse
DashboardConfigResponse.description:
What the dashboard's pickers can offer, and what to chart by default.

The selection is not persisted server-side: the client sends `metric_keys` on the trends request
and owns the user's choice. `evaluator_metric_keys` is a deterministic default so a client with
no stored selection still renders a populated chart.

`available_evaluator_metrics` is the org's whole scorer registry, deliberately *not* the set of
keys seen in the window — a window-derived list changes size with the time range, so the same org
offered 5 evaluators at 7 days and 45 at 90. The defaults stay window-derived, so they chart
evaluators that actually ran.

`available_log_streams` covers every stream in the selected projects and is deliberately *not*
narrowed by the request's own `log_stream_ids` — otherwise picking a stream would collapse the
picker to that one entry and the user could never widen the selection again.

`available_projects` is the picker's own source of truth rather than the host's paginated project
list, which would silently omit projects past its first page — including ones holding data.

DecisionBooleanCriteria.description: What a true answer and a false answer mean, for a yes/no question. The two are set together.

DecisionChoice.description:
One option of a choice question, with an optional description of when it applies.

Extra fields are forbidden, so a level, which has a ``level`` field, never validates as a choice.

DecisionIntegration.description: Providers that serve decision models only. LLM providers keep their `LLMIntegration` value.

DecisionScorerDB.title: DecisionScorerDB
DecisionScorerDB.description:
A row of the decision_scorers table.

answer_options depends on the output type of the scorer:
- categorical: a list of DecisionChoice, or a list of labels (list[str]) for older versions.
- discrete: a list of DecisionLevel.
- boolean_probability: a DecisionBooleanCriteria, or None when the question has no criteria.

DecisionScorerTestConfiguration.title: DecisionScorerTestConfiguration
DecisionScorerTestConfiguration.description:
The evaluator settings of a decision Test request, the same place as the LLM scorer_configuration.

scoreable_node_types holds exactly one node type. input_type defaults to the decision default
for it (get_decision_input_type).

DecisionScorerValidationMetadata.title: DecisionScorerValidationMetadata
DecisionScorerValidationMetadata.description:
What a real decision result writes besides its rating, as the Test tab shows it.

``confidence`` and ``probabilities`` are the fields of the ``{key}_metadata`` metric. The rest are the
values that the real scorer writes under their own metric keys (``_model_alias``, ``_input_tokens``,
``_total_tokens`` and ``_metric_cost``).

DecisionScorerValidationResult.title: DecisionScorerValidationResult
DecisionScorerValidationResult.description:
The task result of a successful manual decision test.

A decision evaluator has no rationale, so the result has a ``rating`` and ``metadata`` and no explanation.
``rating`` is P(yes) for a boolean_probability output, the label for a categorical output, and the
most likely level for a discrete output.

EnvironmentTier.title: EnvironmentTier
EnvironmentTier.description:
Which execution environment serves a scorer version.

``standard`` is the platform-curated set baked into the executor image, so
it has no ``environments`` row -- but it does have a hash, the digest of
the pin list the image was built from. ``custom`` is resolved on demand and
gets a content-addressed row plus a warm parent of its own.

EvaluatorMetricOption.title: EvaluatorMetricOption
EvaluatorMetricOption.description:
One entry in the dashboard's evaluator picker.

`group_label` is the metric's category — "Output Quality", "Agent Quality" and so on — carried
straight from the shared column metadata so the picker can group 70+ options the same way the rest
of the product does. `None` for an evaluator whose definition sets no category.

ExtendedReadSessionRecordWithChildren.title: ExtendedReadSessionRecordWithChildren
ExtendedReadSessionRecordWithChildren.description:
Read-side session response that also accepts synthesized stub_trace roots.

Same shape as ExtendedSessionRecordWithChildren, except `traces` allows the
StubTraceRecord placeholder produced by create_tree_for_extended_read_session
for spans whose TraceRecord hasn't arrived yet. Defined independently of
ExtendedSessionRecordWithChildren/RecordWithChildTraces rather than
subclassing them, since widening their Sequence[ExtendedTraceRecordWithChildren]
field to also allow StubTraceRecord in a subclass is an LSP violation mypy
correctly rejects.

NumericColorConstraint-Output.title: NumericColorConstraint
NumericColorConstraint-Output.description:
A color constraint for numeric metric values.

Assigns a color when a numeric score matches the given operator and value.

Operators and expected value shapes:
  - eq, gt, gte, lt, lte: value must be a single float.
  - between: value must be a list of exactly 2 floats [low, high] where low < high.
    The range is inclusive on both ends.

Example:
    {"color": "green", "operator": "gte", "value": 0.8}
    {"color": "yellow", "operator": "between", "value": [0.3, 0.7]}

ScorerMultimodalCapabilitiesFilter.title: ScorerMultimodalCapabilitiesFilter
ScorerMultimodalCapabilitiesFilter.description:
Filter scorers by multimodal_capabilities.

Use operator ``contains`` to match scorers that support a single capability
(e.g. ``{"name": "multimodal_capabilities", "operator": "contains", "value": "vision"}``).
Use ``one_of`` to match scorers whose capabilities include ANY of the given
values (e.g. ``{"name": "multimodal_capabilities", "operator": "one_of", "value": ["vision", "audio"]}``).
``text`` is a filter-only value supplied in the ``one_of`` list
(e.g. ``{"operator": "one_of", "value": ["text"]}``) that matches scorers
with no multimodal capabilities.

SectionEnvelope.title: SectionEnvelope
SectionEnvelope.description:
One section's worth of cards plus the metadata describing how complete it is.

Availability semantics are frozen:

- at least one card succeeded → `available=True`; `data_status` is `complete` when every card
  succeeded and `partial` when some did not.
- every card failed → `available=False`, `data_status=unavailable`, and section-level `degraded`
  is set from the most common card failure. Cards remain in the payload with their own
  `degraded` payloads.

TokenomicsForecastResultsV1Request.title: TokenomicsForecastResultsV1Request
TokenomicsForecastResultsV1Request.description:
Forward-looking, bucketed read. ``filters.time_range.start_date`` is ignored -- the series
always begins today (or later, if the stored forecast is stale); only ``end_date`` optionally
caps how far out it runs. Fiscal period resolution uses dates the service computes itself
(see TokenomicsService.get_forecast_results), not the caller's start_date -- which is why this
does not reuse the shared ``_validate_fiscal_trend_interval`` validator usage/adoption trends
use: that validator requires a full time_range for a fiscal interval, because those endpoints
are reading a historical, caller-defined window. Forecast has no such window.

``filters`` uses the fiscal-capable filters, so ``time_range`` has no window cap. The 128-day
horizon already bounds the response. A fiscal-year-to-date request runs from today to the year's
end, and in a 53-week fiscal year that range can exceed the 366-day read cap.

``leader_user_key`` is deliberately accepted under BOTH views, matching
/tokenomics/v1/team-rollup: it selects which team's forecast to read, while ``view`` selects
which authorization rule proves the caller may read it (organization view -> any manager in
the directory; team view -> only managers inside the caller's own subtree). Requiring
view="team" would force every team read down the team branch, which resolves the caller's own
directory identity -- locking out an organization admin who is not a mapped worker, and
limiting a mapped manager to their own subtree. See _resolve_forecast_effective_scope, which
asks resolve_scope for a directory whenever a leader_user_key is present so the organization
view still arrives with directory_generation_id set.

No ``custom`` interval (no caller-supplied bucket boundaries) and no real ``group_by``
breakdown -- ``group_by`` accepts only ``"total"`` today, reserved for a future per-provider/
model forecast.

TokenomicsForecastResultsV1Response.title: TokenomicsForecastResultsV1Response
TokenomicsForecastResultsV1Response.description:
``unavailable_reason`` says why ``result`` is null, so the UI can explain a missing forecast.

``not_available`` covers every case without a stored row for the scope: the sweep has not run
yet, the run failed, or the team is too small to forecast.

api__schemas__scorer__CategoricalColorCo.title: CategoricalColorConstraint
api__schemas__scorer__CategoricalColorCo.description:
A color constraint for categorical or multi-label metric values.

Assigns a color when a categorical score matches the given operator and value.

Operators and expected value shapes:
  - eq: value must be a single string.
  - one_of: value must be a list of strings.

Example:
    {"color": "green", "operator": "eq", "value": "pass"}
    {"color": "red", "operator": "one_of", "value": ["fail", "error"]}

api__schemas__scorer__NumericColorConstr.title: NumericColorConstraint
api__schemas__scorer__NumericColorConstr.description:
A color constraint for numeric metric values.

Assigns a color when a numeric score matches the given operator and value.

Operators and expected value shapes:
  - eq, gt, gte, lt, lte: value must be a single float.
  - between: value must be a list of exactly 2 floats [low, high] where low < high.
    The range is inclusive on both ends.

Example:
    {"color": "green", "operator": "gte", "value": 0.8}
    {"color": "yellow", "operator": "between", "value": [0.3, 0.7]}

libs__python__schemas__log_records__feed.title: TreeChoiceConstraints
libs__python__schemas__log_records__feed.description:
Tree-choice node values must be globally unique leaf-path values.

Callers that start from nested YAML should use build_tree_choice_nodes_from_yaml
so duplicate ids or labels in different branches are converted to unambiguous
slash-delimited path values before model validation.

name.title: Name
name.description: The model name used when calling the API.

alias.title: Alias
alias.description: The display name/alias for the model. Defaults to name.

based_on.title: Based On
based_on.description: Alias of a built-in model whose parameter map should be used. For example, 'gpt-5.4'. Mutually exclusive with supported_parameters.

supported_parameters.title: Supported Parameters
supported_parameters.description: Explicit list of parameter names this model supports (e.g., ['max_tokens', 'temperature', 'verbosity']). Each name must be a valid RunParamsMap field. Mutually exclusive with based_on.

supports_json_schema.title: Supports Json Schema
supports_json_schema.description: Set to true only if the endpoint supports OpenAI-style structured outputs for this model. When true, Galileo sends JSON response schemas, such as those of LLM-as-a-judge metrics, as response_format with type 'json_schema'. Works with based_on and with supported_parameters.

promptgalileo__schemas__config__custom__.title: ModelProperties
promptgalileo__schemas__config__custom__.description:
Properties for a model in a custom integration.

Attributes:
    name: The model name used when calling the API.
    alias: The display name/alias for the model in the UI.
          Defaults to ``name`` when not provided.
    based_on: Alias of a built-in model whose parameter map should be used.
              Mutually exclusive with ``supported_parameters``.
    supported_parameters: Explicit list of parameter names this model supports.
                          Mutually exclusive with ``based_on``.
    supports_json_schema: Whether the endpoint supports an OpenAI-style ``json_schema``
                          ``response_format`` for this model. Defaults to False.
